questions_for_advisor: The breach is worth more than its repair. The contract that a response precedes the next command was landed by the executor itself under ARCH-20260919-007, and the executor then broke it in the same session, on the single most consequential run of the arc — and did not notice. It was caught by the advisor reading the responses directory, which is exactly the surface AGENTS.md says is the advisor's only view. **The channel's safety property is that somebody reads it, and that is not a guard.** If the advisor wants it enforced rather than observed, the mechanism is the same shape as ARCH-20260920-006's: a check that a command's parent has a response before the command may execute. That is a ruling, and it is the natural sibling of the preconditions schema.

A reconstruction is weaker evidence than a contemporaneous record and the file says so. What it cannot recover is what the executor believed at the time — the IN_PROGRESS commit's whole evidentiary purpose. Nothing in the durable record distinguishes a response written before the work from one written after it, which is why the rule exists.
